74246511.b:
The historic palaces in Tabab

The Al Abu Noghta Al Mutahami palaces, overlooking the banks of Wadi Tahlal, stand out as one of the most important palaces of the historic village of Tabab. They consist of 6 sites built of mountain rock stone, of varying heights over an area of 4,000 meters, while the beauty of their windows and the upper edges of the palaces, in white that blends with the clouds that occasionally surprise visitors, stands out.

You can see the eight silos built into the rocky mountain, which the locals used in the past to store and preserve grain. The rock does not absorb water when rain falls, and the silos extend to a depth of 3 meters, while their width reaches 16 meters.

The palaces offer a range of facilities, including restaurants with outdoor seating overlooking the village and its farms, service kiosks and shops for souvenirs, and a bakery for tasting fresh southern bread from the hot tannour.

To experience staying in the Al Abu Noghta Al Mutahami palaces, you can book one of their suites, prepared for moments that find their way into your memory.

68625975.s: Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque (may God be pleased with him) is one of the most important archaeological mosques of the Islamic era. Its importance stems from its layout, which continues the planning pattern of the first mosques in Islam, in the manner of the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah in its early stages. The mosque is famous for its minaret, considered the first minaret built in Islam, with a stone height of about 12 meters, from which the call to prayer was given.
68625975.b:
Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque (may God be pleased with him) is one of the most important archaeological mosques of the Islamic era. Its importance stems from its layout, which continues the planning pattern of the first mosques in Islam, in the manner of the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah in its early stages. The mosque is famous for its minaret, considered the first minaret built in Islam, with a stone height of about 12 meters, from which the call to prayer was given.

Historical Background

The historical importance of Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque comes from a number of accounts that attribute its construction to the second caliph, Omar ibn Al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him), who ordered it built on his return from Jerusalem in 17 AH.
